Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! Thomas Rew has some last words with his teammates in the huddle before they disperse to take their respective fielding positions. Sameer Minhas and Mohammad Shayan will open the inning for Pakistan Under-19. Sebastian Morgan will start with the new ball with two slip fielders. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The target is 211 on the board. It is not a big target, but folks, the track surely has something for the bowlers. It's no doubt a hard pitch, but there are some patches where the ball skids low, and if the English bowlers exploit those, then Pakistan's batting unit has some work to do on this second inning. Stick around with us as the second essay will commence any time!

Abdul Subhan from Pakistan Under-19 says that the wicket was helping the spinners and reckons every wicket in Zimbabwe tends to be spin-friendly. Adds that the captain and coach asked him to focus on dot balls and that's what he did out there, and they got the reward for it as well. Mentions that they have 4-5 amazing fielders in the squad, and they compete amongst each other as to who will get more catches and run outs. Ends by saying that he likes to sing, and sometimes he performs for his teammates.

After that, the set batter who notched up his fifty, Caleb Falconer (66 off 73 balls), was dismissed by Ali Raza just after three overs, and after that event, no real threat was proposed from England Under-19, and they ended up putting 210 runs. If we talk about Pakistan's bowlers, they were simply outstanding. After winning the toss, the bowlers may have been a bit wayward with the new ball but they came back strongly, and for that reason, the opposition batters couldn't swing away their bat to hit big. Tight fielding also suffocated the opposition from rotating the strikes and put them under pressure. By the end of the inning, Ahmed Hussain bagged three wickets, and Ali Raza, Abdul Subhan, and Momin Qamar picked up two scalps each.

The English batters had a cautious start, yet the Pakistan Under-19 bowlers got the wickets at the right time. Usually, we have seen bright young pacers coming from the Pakistan camp, but Ahmed Hussain showed that there are some real quality spinners as well. It was Hussain and Ali Raza who shook hands to clear the English top order. England Under-19 were 90 for 4 in the 19th over, and just when they wanted a batter who could play a long knock, they had it in the shape of Caleb Falconer, whereas Ralphie Albert provided the supporting role. They both had a partnership of 80, but Hussain stepped up for Pakistan and ended the most crucial partnership by eliminating Albert.

It was an outstanding bowling effort, and we can fairly say that Pakistan Under-19 have got a bit of an upper hand in the contest! Not only did they bowl well, but the fielding was very sharp as well. It was not a bad inning for England Under-19, especially on this tough pitch, but if they could have added more 30-40 runs to the 210 scoreline, skipper Thomas Rew would have been even more satisfied.

Farhan Ahmed of England Under-19 also shared a few words. He says that it is great to be back and the preparation has been great with this team. Mentions that captaining the side in the Caribbean has helped him gain good experience, and they have a well-balanced side. Ends by saying that he just wants to contribute to the team's success.

Ali Raza of Pakistan Under-19 is up for a quick chat. He says that this is the stage where a player starts his journey. Adds that he is excited to be part of it once again. Mentions that they missed out in the semi-final last time, but this time want to go all the way. Says he has worked hard to improve his skills and is looking forward to the challenges ahead.

Now Andy Flower brings the attention is on the track and starts off saying that the deck is hard and dry, therefore it will provide some bounce and the new ball will offer some swing with the help of the wind.

Thomas Rew, the captain of England Under-19, says that they would have bowled first and hopes the weather stays away. Adds they won the first two warm-up games but also had a good week of practice before this game and are ready to take down Pakistan. Says that they excited and the team is in a good spot. Ends by saying that they have two spinners who can bat as well, and a couple of fiery fast bowlers.

Farhan Yousaf, skipper of Pakistan Under-19, says that they checked the conditions first and opted to bowl first. Informs that the tri series and the warm up matches were really effective for them prior the tournament. A fascinating contest beckons at the Takashinga Sports Club in Harare as Pakistan Under-19 face England Under-19 in Match 4 of the ICC Under-19 World Cup 2026, with both sides keen to make an early statement in the group. England arrive still searching for a return to past glory, having not won the tournament since their title triumph in 1997/98, but the current squad, led by Thomas Rew, carries plenty of promise and balance. Rew comes into the tournament in good touch, having shone with an unbeaten 71 in a rain-affected warm-up game against India, a match England went on to win, offering an early glimpse of their resilience and composure. With batters like Ben Dawkins, Joe Moores and Will Bennison providing solidity and intent, and variety in the bowling department through Farhan Ahmed, Manny Lumsden and Alex French, England will look to rely on structure, discipline and sustained pressure. Pakistan, on the other hand, bring a rich Under-19 pedigree into the contest, having gone back-to-back in 2003/04 and 2005/06, the only team to achieve consecutive titles at this level. Skipper Farhan Yousaf marshals a side brimming with confidence, having already led this group to glory at the Under-19 Asia Cup just last month, destroying arch rivals India in the final, and the decision to retain a strong core from that triumph means several players arrive with the experience of winning silverware and a hunger for more. The sings were encouraging in the warm-ups as well, with Sameer Minhas striking a fluent fifty against USA, who also scored a magnificent 172 against India in that final, while Ali Hasan Baloch underlined his attacking credentials with a fiery 36 off just 19 balls. With batting depth through Usman Khan, Minhas and Ahmed Hussain and bowling strength built around pace and penetration from the likes of Ali Raza, Daniyal Ali Khan and Ali Raza, Pakistan will back their natural aggression to make the difference. There is some rain forecast around Harare, but both sides will be hopeful the weather stays out of the way, allowing this clash between England’s method and Pakistan’s instinctive flair to unfold in full.
